Done. The app is running in the background on port 3000.

## What I built

`/home/agent/todo-app/` — plain Node, zero dependencies (only `http`, `fs`, `path`, `crypto` from stdlib):

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `server.js` | HTTP server + REST API + static file serving |
| `public/index.html` | App markup |
| `public/app.js` | Client logic (vanilla JS, `fetch`) |
| `public/style.css` | Styling (dark/light via `prefers-color-scheme`) |
| `todos.json` | Created on first write; persists tasks across restarts |

## Features

- Add, complete, edit (double-click text), and delete tasks
- Filters: All / Active / Done, plus "Clear done"
- Live summary count, empty states, path-traversal guard on static serving

## API

```
GET    /api/todos              list
POST   /api/todos              { "text": "..." } → create
PATCH  /api/todos/:id          { "done": true } and/or { "text": "..." }
DELETE /api/todos/:id          remove one
DELETE /api/todos/completed    remove all done
GET    /health                 liveness
```

## Status

- PID **241**, listening on `0.0.0.0:3000`, logging to `/home/agent/todo-app/server.log`
- Verified: `/health` → `{"status":"ok","todos":0}`, create/list/delete all working, `/` returns `200 text/html`

Since you're making the link yourself, I left the port as-is and didn't publish anything. If you'd rather I publish it through the sandbox runtime instead, say the word and I'll run `tangle preview publish --port 3000`.

One note: the server binds `0.0.0.0` and has no auth, so anyone who can reach the URL can read and modify the list — fine for a demo, worth adding a check before sharing widely.
